days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday belongs to the fair and the South End. The Champlain Valley Fair runs noon to 10 in Essex Junction today and adult admission drops to $10 after 5, then ZZ Top with George Thorogood & the Destroyers ($39-69) take the grandstand at 6 with doors at 5. Down on Pine Street, the organizers say tonight is the last South End Get Down of the summer , so swing through the block party between 5 and 9 for one more lap of the food trucks and a goodbye to your favorite vendors. Over in South Burlington, the South Burlington Farmers Market sets up on the airport rec path from 5 to 7 with Bart Feller playing, and the first 75 households through get $5 in market spending money. The Waterfront Silent Disco ($25) meets at 6 at 1 College Street in front of ECHO, headphones on, dancing along the water. Music people have a free night if they want one. New York cosmic soul act Lady Moon & The Eclipse plays Foam at 9 with Beccs opening, free and all ages, and Alligator Wine plays a free Dancing in the Streets set on the Skinny Pancake waterfront patio from 8 to 11, while 90 Proof plays the Spanked Puppy in Colchester Friday evening. Punk Rock Queer Prom ($10) fills the Light Club Lamp Shop at 8 with four bands, Cat Crash, the Eyetraps, Emo Girls Kissing and We're Here! To Kill, 21 plus. Comedy fans, Matthew Broussard's 7 PM shows at Vermont Comedy Club ($30) are sold out both nights, but the 9 PM shows Friday and Saturday still have seats. And a heads up for anyone hoping to catch Sierra Ferrell on the green at Shelburne Museum tonight, the show is sold out and Higher Ground's waitlist and ticket exchange are the only ways in.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday is the fullest day of the weekend, and we are out in it. Our own BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] takes the big outdoor table Zero Gravity at 10, no agenda, just coffee and good conversation, and then a bunch of us are heading to the fair. Btown at the Champlain Valley Fair [MEETUP] meets at 1 at Expo North, the first big building after you come in through the Red Gate by the parking lot. Weekend admission is $20, an unlimited ride bracelet is $40 and parking is $10 a car, so carpool if you can, and come eat fried things with us. Pine Street does its market double header, the Burlington Farmers Market from 9 to 2 at 345 Pine, and the Burlington Vintage Market Fall Flea right next door at Barge Canal, also 9 to 2, with 15 plus dealers of vintage clothing, vinyl and $5 piles. South Burlington goes big. Park Fest spreads nine acts across five parks from 1 to 4:15 with a passport you stamp at each stop for prizes and free shuttles running between them, then the International Food Festival ($35) at Veterans Memorial Park from 5:30 to 7:30 buys five tasting plates from vendors of your choice, and everyone attending has to register. Saturday night, Bow Wow, Soulja Boy and Fat Joe ($39-69) headline the grandstand at 7 with doors at 5:30, Emoji Nightmare's Pride Ball ($35-40) fills the Higher Ground Ballroom with Drag Race All Stars winner Angeria Paris VanMichaels and King of Drag winner King Molasses under a Denim & Diamonds theme, doors 7:30, 18 plus, and Pile's Rick Maguire plays Radio Bean at 8 with Vehicle, one of the last shows there before the Bean closes next week . Also Saturday, Wild Inside ($12) , the film about Flaco, the owl who escaped the Central Park Zoo and lived wild in Manhattan, screens at VTIFF at 1 and again at 3, Soup for Two and Salmo ($10) play indie folk at the Venetian Soda Lounge from 7 to 9, Josh Panda brings his southern soul rock and roll to Foam at 9 for free, three indie folk bands play the Odd Fellows hall on North Ave from 6:30 to 10, and Queeraoke with Lizzie Murderz keeps Standing Stone Wines in Winooski singing Saturday night. Mountain bikers, VMBA Days at Bolton runs 10 to 4 with guided rides, downhill clinics, a dual slalom and a Lawson's Finest après.

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday is the clearest day of the weekend and the fair's last. The final day of the Champlain Valley Fair runs 10 to 10, and Night Ranger and John Waite ($39-69) close out the grandstand at 7 with doors at 5:30, and tickets bought before show day include fair admission. Alabama Shakes with Emily King at Shelburne Museum at 7 is sold out, waitlist and official exchange only. Sunday Night Mass ($30-38) brings Toronto house and techno producer Sydney Blu to the Showcase Lounge with Maus and Valkyrie, doors 7:30, 18 plus. Daytime is easy. The Winooski Farmers Market runs 10 to 2 on Winooski Falls Way, Sunset Watchers Club is partying at the free, family friendly Sunday Session at Four Quarters Brewing in Winooski from 1 to 8 with four DJs, and the Sunday Polo Match ($10-20) at Amdez Polo Club in Shelburne goes tailgate style at 3 with gates at 2:30, so bring a chair. Dads can drop into the Dad Guild Run Club on the bike path at 7:30 AM, dads only. Board gamers get Mix & Mingle [MEETUP] at The Boardroom from 12 to 5, letter writers have the new monthly Burlington Letter Writing Group at Zero Gravity from 10 to 11, crafters have Crafternoons at the Odd Fellows hall from 3 to 5, and the LGBTQIA+ Women's Dance at the St. John's Club runs 4 to 8 with DJ Corey, lake views and a cash bar, $15-20 suggested donation.
